assertions.text: Every @TableTest function is declared inside a type (a struct, class, enum or an extension of one), not at file scope.
Test function body contains no if, guard or switch statement and no ternary
No @TableTest function body defaults a value with ??, or calls .map, .flatMap or .compactMap on one of its parameters.
Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Result?')

A switch, an if or guard that compares with a case, or a ternary on a case, of a test-local enum with String raw values is in a member of that enum (the enum itself or an extension of it), never in another function of the test type that takes the enum or reads a property of its type.

Each of the three refusals has its own row, or its own value-set member, with its reason in an expectation cell: the poll is closed (pollClosed), the voter has no vote in the box (noVoteToReplace), the voter's ballot is sealed (ballotSealed). FAILS when a reason has no case.

A refused case asserts the state of the box after the call — the voter's vote (vote(of:)) and the tally — read from the box, in addition to the returned refusal. FAILS when a refused case asserts only the returned value.

The state after a refusal is asserted in one of three forms: a table that also has a row where the state changes (the accepted replacement); one row with a value set of the refusal reasons; or a before-state column whose cells differ between the refused rows, so that the after-state column differs too. FAILS when an after-state column (the voter's vote or the tally after the call) has the same cell in every row of a table with two or more rows, and when the unchanged state is asserted with a constant in the test body.

The refusal reason is an expectation cell (such as refused(pollClosed), or a Refusal column), and the replaced and refused rows share one assertion. FAILS when the body chooses what to assert by a branch, or when the refusal is a constant in the body rather than a cell.
No init(from:) is written into the app code under Sources/.
swift build --build-tests succeeds against the package scaffolding
